---
title: "Common withholding cost and matched disclosure"
subtitle: "3.8 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 16–17"
description: "Risk comparisons at a common cost and error comparisons at a common disclosure level."
---

Two comparisons use different constraints. At a common withholding cost, posterior risk combines expected errors
with the cost of the pairs left unstated. At matched disclosure, the frontier comparison holds the number of stated
pairs fixed and compares expected wrong counts. The display evaluates the same rules under both criteria, using one
posterior and a specified report family. This makes the source of each risk or error difference explicit. For the
thirty-unit example, the boundary is restricted to contiguous cuts of one order.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same τ, .20.** Posterior-mean tiers state 21 pairs with risk .1612, while the best report states 17 with risk
  .1455. These reports disclose different amounts. The solid and dashed lines have the same slope; a lower line
  has lower risk at this τ.
- **Same N, eight units.** The tiers' gap is .1634 at N 21. The diamond is a frontier mixture, while the square
  marks the best single report at that N. The table now compares wrong counts at each rule's own disclosure.
- **Thirty units, one order.** The capped family has 436 reports. Posterior-mean tiers state 300 pairs with E 48.31.
  The boundary is optimal within this order; other orders are not searched.
- **Thirty units, same τ.** Without the cap, the family contains 536,870,912 contiguous cuts of the posterior-mean order. There is no enumerated cloud here. Both comparison modes use the same units.
- **Flags outside the order.** The flag report is outside this family: it still has an evaluated risk, but no matched-disclosure
  benchmark in this order family. The hollow mark records this restriction.
- **All-withheld.** N is 0 and the risk at τ .20 is .2000. Its fraction of stated pairs that are wrong is undefined.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
All rules share a supplied normal teaching posterior. Flags use the mean of all thirty estimates as their reference.
On thirty units the boundary is the hull of contiguous cuts in one declared order, not the unrestricted H(m).
Changing τ changes the loss; changing the family changes the benchmark. Risks across those settings answer
different questions. No reporting-risk comparison establishes a rule's value for allocation or classification.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}

The package's synthetic `pr_example_gaussian` poverty example uses its own thirty sites. At τ .25 with at most four
grades, this prints quantile cuts with N 337 and risk .1758, versus optimal cuts with N 303 and risk .1603. The risks correspond to different N; H(m) is not a package output.

```r
w <- c(poverty=1, frl=0, snap=0); s <- postrank_settings(weights=w, tau=.25, G_max=4L); sc <- pr_example_gaussian$means[, "poverty"]
sapply(c("quantile", "optimal"), function(r) unlist(postrank_cuts(sc, pr_example_gaussian, s, direction="descending", rule=r)$evaluation[c("N", "primary_risk")]))
```

:::
